name: Mento Canadian Dollar
oneLiner: CADm is Mento's Canadian dollar stablecoin on Celo, minted CDP-style against USDm collateral (Mento V3, a Liquity v2 fork).
collateral: Mento V3 Liquity-v2-style CDPs collateralized by USDm; USDm in turn is backed by the diversified Mento Reserve mix (sUSDS, CELO, EURC, USDC, USDT, axlEUROC, stETH, and smaller positions exposed via the Mento reserve dashboard).
pegMechanism: Mento V3 oracle-priced FX stablecoin minted by depositing USDm as CDP collateral and borrowing CADm against it; user-set interest rates, Stability Pool liquidations, and Liquity-style redemptions support the CADm peg, with circuit breakers and Mento reserve transparency on the upstream USDm leg.

oracleRisk.summary: CADm's live Celo USDm/CADm Broker exchange uses one SortedOracles reporter with a 360-second report-expiry window and minimumReports set to one; BreakerBox gates the swap but no second feed or failover path is configured.

branchApplicability.rationale: At Celo block 72127154, CADm broker() returned the Mento v2 Broker and BiPoolManager exposed one USDm/CADm exchange using rate feed 0x20869cF54Ead821C45DFb2aB0C23d2e10Fbb65A4, minimumReports 1, and a 360-second reset/expiry window. SortedOracles had one reporter for that feed. The current Mento reserve API lists active CDP troves only for GBPm, JPYm, and CHFm, not CADm, so CADm has no live borrower-specific oracle/liquidation branch to enumerate.

blacklistabilityReview.evidence: The Celo explorer resolves the tracked CADm proxy to verified StableTokenV2 implementation 0x434563B0604BE100F04B7Ae485BcafE3c9D8850E. The reviewed implementation exposes standard stable-token transfer operations but no holder blacklist, freeze, or pause function. CADm retains inherited exposure from the Mento reserve mix, including freezable upstream stablecoins such as USDC, USDT, and EURC.

mintAuthority.summary: CADm is minted via the Mento Broker (0x777A...) which is the sole authorized minter (broker() getter confirmed). The Broker's proxy admin and the CADm token owner and proxy admin all resolve to the Mento Timelock (0x890DB...) with a 2-day delay.

controls.label: Mento Broker — authorized minter for CADm
controls.evidence: At Celo block 69287341, broker() on CADm (0xff4ab19391af240c311c54200a492233052b6325) returned 0x777A8255cA72412f0d706dc03C9D1987306B4CaD (Mento BrokerProxy). The Broker's EIP-1967 proxy admin slot returned 0x890DB8A597940165901372Dd7DB61C9f246e2147 (Mento Timelock).

controls.label: Mento Timelock — CADm token owner and proxy admin
controls.evidence: At Celo block 69287341, owner() on CADm returned 0x890DB8A597940165901372Dd7DB61C9f246e2147; EIP-1967 proxy admin slot returned the same address. getMinDelay() on the Timelock returned 0x2a300 = 172800 seconds (48 hours).

review.evidence: At Celo block 69287341: owner() = Timelock 0x890DB8A597940165901372Dd7DB61C9f246e2147 (confirmed); EIP-1967 proxy admin slot = same Timelock; getMinDelay() = 172800s (48h); broker() = 0x777A8255cA72412f0d706dc03C9D1987306B4CaD (Mento BrokerProxy, confirmed as sole authorized minter); Broker EIP-1967 proxy admin = same Timelock. Celo Registry confirms Broker = 0x777A... All mint-capable surfaces resolved. Economically, Broker issuance is the collateral-exchange path; changing that path or authorizing different mint logic requires the independently enforced 48-hour Mento Timelock, so the encoding-derived unbounded cap is superseded by raiseable semantics.

bridgeRouteRisk.summary: CADm is tracked only on Celo in Pharos and Mento docs route users to Celo-native Mento stables. No material bridge route is present for the reviewed metadata row.
